source_caption:
The iconic speech in Gladiator wasn’t fully locked before filming. Russell Crowe worked closely with director Ridley Scott to shape the wording and delivery, turning it into one of the most powerful and quoted monologues in modern cinema.

Gladiator (2000), directed by Ridley Scott, starring Russell Crowe, Joaquin Phoenix, Connie Nielsen. An epic tale of vengeance and honor that follows a betrayed Roman general who rises as a gladiator to confront the emperor who destroyed his life.

source_details.title: Gladiator
source_details.synopsis: Gladiator is a 2000 epic action adventure drama film directed by Ridley Scott and written by David Franzoni, John Logan, and William Nicholson from a story by Franzoni. It stars Russell Crowe, Joaquin Phoenix, Connie Nielsen, Oliver Reed, Derek Jacobi, Djimon Hounsou, and Richard Harris. Crowe portrays Maximus Decimus Meridius, a Roman general who is betrayed when Commodus, the ambitious son of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, murders his father and seizes the throne. Reduced to a slave, Maximus becomes a gladiator and rises through the ranks of the arena, determined to avenge the murders of his family and the emperor.
